A selected-node change is reflected or invalidates the plan before apply.
evidence: Selected node identities/resourceVersions and classification evidence.
Plan comparison before/after each scope change.
adapter_requirements: Explain output identifying which nodes contributed evidence.
cases.acceptance: The valid pool request remains valid despite outside-pool sharing; selected-node mutations cannot be silently ignored.

cases.title: Recognize MPS and mixed or incomplete sharing evidence
given: Independent fixtures include explicit sharing-strategy=mps without replicas/SHARED suffix, time-slicing, MIG, whole-device and unlabeled advertisers.
Requested contract distinguishes physical whole GPUs, a share, and hardware-isolated MIG.
fault_schedule: Classify each fixture and mixed eligible-node combinations.
Request two distinct physical GPUs against each classified pool.
Remove auxiliary labels while preserving explicit MPS evidence.
assertions: MPS is not classified as whole-device exclusive solely because auxiliary labels are missing.
Unknown or contradictory eligible-node evidence does not silently upgrade the contract to physical exclusivity.
Valid homogeneous whole-device pools still admit multi-GPU requests.
evidence: Fixture source/version, normalized evidence and contract decisions.
User-visible unsupported/unknown reason.
adapter_requirements: Capability vocabulary includes whole, MIG, MPS, time-sliced and unknown.
Explicit operator override, if supported, is logged as an override rather than inferred fact.
cases.acceptance: No fixture with known sharing or unresolved evidence is certified as a two-physical-GPU grant; whole-device positive controls pass.

cases.title: Detect per-host fragmentation before claiming a whole-GPU plan is feasible
given: Two hosts each have three free physical GPUs; three replicas each need two GPUs on one host.
Positive controls include three hosts with two free GPUs and two replicas on the original hosts.
fault_schedule: Compute feasibility and compare with an independent exhaustive small-instance bin-packing oracle.
Generate small inventories/demands with identical totals and maxima but different packability.
assertions: The 3+3 / three-times-2 request is not reported fully schedulable.
A returned placement is realizable on individual hosts and respects all replicas simultaneously.
If the backend delegates scheduling, it reports pending/infeasible instead of claiming complete admission.
evidence: Oracle assignment or impossibility certificate for generated small cases.
Planner explanation and per-replica device/host assignment.
adapter_requirements: Independent exhaustive oracle limited to bounded small cases.
Admission result separates proposed capacity from scheduler-confirmed allocation.
cases.acceptance: All bounded generated cases agree with the independent oracle and the known 3+3 regression cannot be marked fully feasible.

cases.title: Keep plans isolated across concurrent and failed deployments
given: One long-lived process serves deployments A and B through the registered allocation adapter; they target different flow IDs and inventories.
A succeeds in planning; B can fail validation or contain CPU-only specs.
fault_schedule: Interleave resolve(A), resolve(B), prepare(A), prepare(B); repeat B with a planning exception and no GPU nodes.
Restart a worker carrying only B's operation identifier.
assertions: Each apply uses its own immutable plan, inventory revision and operation ID.
Failed/CPU-only B cannot reuse A's cached layout or exclusion set.
A stale plan is rejected if its inventory/owner prerequisites have changed.
evidence: Plan hashes/IDs and per-operation mutation logs.
Crash/restart input and recovered plan identity.
adapter_requirements: Plan values passed explicitly; no unscoped singleton state.
cases.acceptance: All mutations are attributable to the correct valid plan; failed or CPU-only operations perform no GPU mutation.

cases.title: Prevent foreign allocations arriving between planning and repartitioning
given: An idle MIG-capable node is planned for reconfiguration while another namespace can schedule GPU work there.
A sentinel CUDA process verifies continued access if the foreign workload is admitted.
fault_schedule: Pause before geometry mutation; submit a foreign GPU pod and let the scheduler/API race with allocator exclusion.
Resume allocation after the foreign pod is bound; reverse the order in a second run.
assertions: Either the foreign pod is prevented from binding by an enforceable ownership/admission boundary, or the reconfiguration aborts without disrupting it.
A Videoflow label alone is not treated as a scheduler lock.
Both exclusive-device-plugin and managed-MIG clients obey the same ownership boundary.
evidence: Pod binding/API timeline, ownership epoch and geometry changes.
Sentinel completion plus NVML UUID/context continuity.
adapter_requirements: Dedicated node admission/reservation mechanism or explicit inability to provide this capability.
Real scheduler plus GPU observer; synthetic simultaneous method calls are insufficient.
cases.acceptance: No admitted foreign GPU context is reset by the tested allocation operation in either controlled interleaving.

cases.title: Delay allocation release while retained or terminating workloads still use GPUs
given: A batch or failed worker still holds its GPU after deployment control exits; include an explicit keep-workloads option and a slow terminating process.
fault_schedule: Trigger controller failure/interrupt and cleanup while the pod remains live.
Request deletion, delay kubelet termination/unprepare, then allow the final GPU user to exit.
assertions: Retaining a workload retains its required allocation/geometry.
Cleanup distinguishes deletion requested from process/device release confirmed.
After the final user releases, cleanup completes once and does not affect unrelated allocations.
evidence: Pod UID/lifecycle and allocation reference history.
NVML process/device use plus unprepare or equivalent release acknowledgment.
adapter_requirements: Process termination and kubelet-unprepare barrier injection.
cases.acceptance: No geometry is destroyed or device reassigned while a retained/terminating test workload still holds it; release follows confirmed final use.

cases.title: Make strict local grants truthful under insufficient GPU count
given: A child process requests two distinct GPUs on a host exposing one; another fixture has more one-GPU workers than devices.
Local strict and explicitly best-effort sharing policies are separate capabilities.
fault_schedule: Start the workload in strict mode; repeat in explicitly opted-in shared/degraded mode.
Test an empty visible pool and a GPU-discovery command failure.
assertions: Strict mode fails before launching a worker with a short or shared grant.
Discovery failure is not reported as a confirmed zero-GPU machine.
Opted-in degradation reports actual devices and sharing; requested GPU count is not presented as delivered capacity.
evidence: Launcher records and child environment/runtime enumeration.
Policy decision and requested versus delivered grant report.
adapter_requirements: Local admission policy and structured delivered-grant object.
Child-process runtime enumeration, not environment inspection alone.
cases.acceptance: Strict mode launches zero under-provisioned GPU workers; degraded mode, when selected, reports exactly the grant observed by each child.

cases.title: Enumerate UUID and MIG grants through the actual CUDA-visible namespace
given: Test masks include GPU UUID, MIG UUID, reordered physical ordinals, empty visibility and container-remapped devices; enumerate only combinations supported by the driver.
fault_schedule: Launch an independent CUDA/NVML probe under each mask and compare its visible usable device count/identity with the allocation adapter.
Run multiple local workers with UUID-pinned parent visibility.
assertions: Valid UUID masks are not reported as no grant.
CUDA indices are local 0..N-1 and resolve to the intended physical/MIG identities.
Unsupported local partitioning is reported before accidental unbounded sharing; an inherited UUID mask is not silently ignored.
evidence: Driver/CUDA versions, original mask and runtime UUID/count output.
Adapter grant and per-child visibility map.
adapter_requirements: CUDA runtime enumeration independent of the adapter.
Capability detection for version-specific multi-MIG enumeration; preserve UUID identity across remapping.
cases.acceptance: For every supported mask the reported grant exactly matches usable CUDA devices; unsupported masks produce an explicit capability result without claiming successful isolation.

cases.title: Admit shared local workers using peak memory and declared guarantees
given: Minimal CUDA worker fixtures have controlled allocations for resident memory, warmup workspace and temporary batch buffers; actual peak bytes are measured independently.
One demand set fits with the configured headroom and another exceeds the shared device budget.
fault_schedule: Start workers concurrently, including synchronized warmup peaks; repeat with a missing or knowingly understated declared memory demand.
Exercise strict admission and explicitly advisory/time-sliced profiles separately.
assertions: Strict admission reserves the aggregate peak budget plus configured headroom before launching all workers.
Advisory/time-sliced modes never advertise a runtime memory isolation guarantee they cannot enforce.
Missing/understated demands are surfaced; measured violations are attributable and do not become silent successful admission evidence.
evidence: Per-process and device-wide memory traces from independent NVML/CUDA measurements.
Admission ledger, declaration provenance and OOM/violation outcomes.
adapter_requirements: Measured memory-profile fixture and explicit advisory versus enforced guarantee metadata.
Configurable headroom and admission budget; no invented model-memory estimate.
cases.acceptance: The over-budget set is rejected in strict mode before concurrent launch; the fitting set runs through measured peak phases within the admitted budget.

cases.title: Consume externally prepared MIG slices without taking over geometry
given: An administrator has preconfigured MIG slices, including a slice used by an unrelated workload; the test requests a compatible free profile.
fault_schedule: Deploy and remove the workload through the static allocation backend.
Restart the application controller, then delete only its allocation/claim.
assertions: Matching externally prepared slices can be requested directly.
Application deploy/teardown neither rejects all foreign geometry nor repartitions/restores the entire node.
Foreign and unused static instance UUIDs persist.
evidence: Before/after NVML instance UUIDs and selected resource/claim.
API/node geometry mutation audit.
adapter_requirements: Static-MIG allocation capability independent of a geometry-management capability.
Read-only NVML observer and API mutation recorder.
cases.acceptance: A compatible free static slice is used successfully and all non-owned geometry survives application lifecycle operations.

cases.title: Keep device-plugin and DRA ownership disjoint
given: A transition environment contains both allocator deployments, with an explicit disjoint node/device ownership map.
A negative configuration attempts to expose the same physical GPU through both inventories.
fault_schedule: Submit independent claims/workloads concurrently through both paths.

For the negative configuration, run capability/admission validation before enabling the second allocator; in an isolated diagnostic environment verify the detector sees duplicate advertised UUID ownership.
assertions: Conflicting allocator ownership is rejected before workload/device preparation.
Valid disjoint pools allocate concurrently without cross-path resets or duplicate grants.
Videoflow managed-MIG hooks never run against DRA-owned nodes.
evidence: ResourceSlice, device-plugin allocation and physical UUID ownership map.
Preparation journal and API mutation audit.
adapter_requirements: Cluster capability inventory records authoritative allocator per device/pool.
Independent UUID-level observer; resource-name inequality is insufficient.
cases.acceptance: No physical GPU is prepared through both allocator paths; invalid overlap fails before enabling workload access.

cases.title: Create independent per-pod DRA claims for independent replicas
given: A stateless stage requests three independently restartable replicas from one ResourceClaimTemplate.
A separate test intentionally scales down and recreates one pod.
fault_schedule: Create replicas concurrently; restart deployment control after only some claims exist.
Delete one pod and recreate it while other replicas continue.
assertions: Each pod owns a distinct ResourceClaim UID generated from the template.
Independent replicas do not accidentally reference one shared claim by template name.
Deleting one replica reclaims only its claim; other claims remain bound and usable.
Controller retries do not leak duplicate unowned claims.
evidence: Pod UID to claim UID owner-reference map and allocation history.
API list/watch trace through deletion/recreation.
adapter_requirements: DRA renderer/application adapter with pod/claim identity access.
Real ResourceClaim controller; a rendered YAML comparison is only a preliminary check.
cases.acceptance: Three live independent replicas have three distinct owned claims, and deletion/recreation does not revoke surviving claims or leave extra orphan claims.

cases.title: Share one allocation only when an explicit execution group requests it
given: Two containers in an intentional execution group share one claim request; two independent pods use separate claims by default.
The grouped and independent designs are declared distinctly in the backend-neutral specification.
fault_schedule: Render and run both designs.
Restart one grouped container, then terminate its pod; separately remove one independent pod.
assertions: Grouped containers reference the same claim request and observe the same intended device allocation.
Independent pods do not share merely because they use the same template.
Group allocation remains while required group consumers exist and releases only at the group's declared lifetime boundary.
evidence: Specification-to-pod-to-claim graph and device identity observations.
Lifecycle events showing claim ownership and last consumer.
adapter_requirements: Explicit execution-group/shared-allocation intent in the deployment adapter.
Device-identity observer and container/pod restart controls.
cases.acceptance: Device sharing exactly follows explicit intent; no independent replica is accidentally coupled to another replica's claim lifetime.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Separate DRA allocation, device preparation and application readiness
given: A ResourceClaim can be scheduler-allocated before the kubelet plugin completes NodePrepareResources and before CUDA/device checks succeed.
fault_schedule: Hold preparation after claim allocation; return transient preparation failures and restart the plugin.
Release preparation, then hold the workload's device-initialization readiness check.
Exercise a permanent unsupported configuration.
assertions: Allocated claim alone never marks the worker or flow ready.
Transient preparation failures retry with the same allocation semantics; permanent failures become actionable failure states.
No downstream deployment success is reported until device preparation and the application's existing readiness contract complete.
evidence: Claim status, Pod conditions, kubelet/plugin RPC log and readiness transitions.
Operation timestamps proving the order of readiness barriers.
adapter_requirements: Fault-injectable DRA plugin/proxy and real kubelet integration.
Readiness adapter distinguishes requested, allocated, prepared and workload-ready states.
cases.acceptance: The worker remains unready throughout both held barriers; retry succeeds once prerequisites complete and permanent preparation failure is surfaced without false readiness.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Reclaim DRA allocations correctly after pod and plugin failures
given: One active claim owns a whole GPU, dynamic MIG instance or MPS group according to the selected profile.
A second unrelated allocation on the same node remains active.
fault_schedule: Crash the workload, restart the GPU kubelet plugin during unprepare, and replay duplicate prepare/unprepare RPCs.
Delete the claim while a finalizer/release operation is delayed; resume after plugin restart.
assertions: Preparation and release are idempotent across duplicate calls and persisted checkpoints.
The device is not reassigned before final release; resources are eventually reusable afterwards.
Dynamic instances/MPS daemons are reclaimed only when their owning allocation no longer needs them.
Unrelated allocations remain usable.
evidence: Claim UID/checkpoint/RPC timeline and independent UUID/context observations.
Before/after resource inventory and orphan resource/daemon count.
adapter_requirements: Real kubelet plus crash/restart injection for the installed DRA release.
cases.acceptance: After recovery all deleted claims release their exclusive resources exactly once with zero orphan instances/daemons, and surviving allocations remain functional.

cases.title: Reject unsupported allocation features before any cluster mutation
given: A versioned capability snapshot states supported allocation type, sharing/isolation guarantees, profile availability and enabled feature gates.
Requests include dynamic MIG on unsupported hardware, MPS plus DynamicMIG, MPS plus active consumable shares and an unsupported multi-device support policy.
fault_schedule: Validate each request with mutation access disabled and then through the full deployment adapter using an audit recorder.
Remove a required capability between plan and apply.
assertions: Unsupported combinations fail before claims, owner labels, policy patches, geometry changes or workload creation.
Messages identify the actual unsupported feature/version/policy rather than asserting a universal hardware impossibility.
A stale capability snapshot is rejected or revalidated before apply.
evidence: Request/capability snapshot and structured validation failure.
Zero-mutation audit and positive-control supported request.
adapter_requirements: Backend-neutral requirement vocabulary plus versioned capabilities.
Validation-before-write boundary enforced by the application adapter.
cases.acceptance: Every unsupported matrix entry is rejected with no side effects; supported controls reach the normal allocation path.

cases.title: Use tested Kubernetes and NVIDIA DRA feature/version combinations
given: Matrix pins NVIDIA DRA v0.5.0, GPU driver, Toolkit, CDI runtime and Kubernetes versions; release docs and API discovery are recorded.
Include base GPU allocation >=1.34.2, 1.34/1.35 with optional upstream gates off/on, and a supported 1.36+ cluster.
fault_schedule: Exercise only requested capabilities: DynamicMIG needs DRAPartitionableDevices on 1.34/1.35; consumable sharing needs DRAConsumableCapacity; MPS requires its driver gate.
Compare release behavior with installed capabilities; never infer support from current main documentation alone.
assertions: Base DRA availability is not mistaken for every optional feature being enabled or production supported.
Missing API fields/gates fail capability validation before resources are written.
GPU allocation experimental/default-off status is surfaced as part of the selected profile, not silently promoted by core DRA GA.
evidence: Cluster API discovery, feature-gate configuration and exact image/chart digests.
Per-capability test result with unsupported cases explicitly distinguished from passing execution tests.
adapter_requirements: Version/capability probe and explicit experimental-profile opt-in.
Real-version matrix runners; unsupported hardware is marked not applicable, never counted as proof of correctness.
cases.acceptance: Each requested capability runs only on a verified supported matrix row; all missing-gate/version negatives fail before mutation with the responsible requirement identified.

cases.title: Reserve consumable GPU capacity across independent claims
given: The installed DRA release publishes multi-allocatable GPU/MIG devices with memory, integer-share or unlimited accounting policies.
Independent claims intentionally overlap one device and their requested totals have fitting and exceeding variants.
fault_schedule: Create claims concurrently at a barrier near the last remaining capacity unit.
Delete one allocation, delay release, then verify a waiting claim can proceed only after capacity returns.
Exercise omitted capacity under memory mode and omitted capacity under unlimited mode.
Submit two claims for the same physical GPU with incompatible driver configuration; compare with matching-configuration control on the pinned release.
assertions: Scheduler accounting never admits claims beyond the published policy for memory/fixed-share modes.
Memory-mode omission consumes the full default advertised memory; unlimited omission is explicitly identified as zero-accounted, unrestricted placement.
Released capacity is reclaimed without double counting.
Independent claims sharing one device obey release-specific configuration compatibility; incompatible settings cannot silently reconfigure another live allocation.
evidence: ResourceSlice requestPolicy, claim consumedCapacity/shareID and scheduler decisions.
Concurrent claim timeline and accounting ledger reconstructed independently from API objects.
adapter_requirements: Independent API accounting oracle; no assumption of runtime isolation.
cases.acceptance: All admitted accounted claims fit the observed policy, blocked claims progress only after release, and unlimited mode is never represented as bounded memory reservation.

cases.title: Distinguish consumable memory accounting from runtime GPU memory isolation
given: Consumable-memory claims share a GPU with declared capacities; a controlled CUDA allocator can request more than its declared scheduler reservation without exhausting the test host.
A separate static-MIG control uses a hardware-isolated slice.
fault_schedule: Run the controlled allocator above its consumable reservation but within safe device limits, observe actual CUDA behavior, and stop at the test safety bound.
Repeat the interface contract check for MIG while querying its actual memory capacity; no test requires intentionally disrupting a co-tenant.
assertions: Consumable profile advertises scheduling accounting and never promises per-process CUDA enforcement.
Measured over-reservation allocations, if accepted by CUDA, are reported as proof that accounting is not isolation rather than backend corruption.
Requests demanding enforced memory isolation are routed to a capable profile or rejected; MIG capacity is independently verified.
evidence: Declared consumedCapacity versus actual successful CUDA bytes.
Capability guarantee report and hardware slice memory observation.
adapter_requirements: Safe bounded CUDA allocation probe on an isolated test device.
Guarantee taxonomy separating scheduler reservation, runtime cap and hardware isolation.
cases.acceptance: No consumable profile claims an enforcement guarantee; an enforced-isolation request is never silently satisfied by scheduler accounting alone.

cases.title: Validate MPS client budgets without claiming throughput isolation
given: Two cooperating CUDA clients intentionally share one DRA claim with configured active-thread percentage and pinned-device-memory limits.
A separate negative request combines MPS with active consumable shares or DynamicMIG.
fault_schedule: Start clients concurrently, verify connection to the claim's daemon, and exercise allocation just below/above the configured per-client memory limit.
Restart one client and then release the final claim consumer.
assertions: Configured MPS limits are applied to the intended clients and reported with their actual scope.
Client restart does not create an unbounded extra daemon; final release reclaims the daemon.
No minimum FPS/latency guarantee is inferred from active-thread percentage.
Unsupported combinations fail before resource preparation.
evidence: MPS daemon configuration, CUDA client allocation results and device identity.
Daemon lifecycle and profile guarantee report.
adapter_requirements: MPS-enabled hardware runner and independent daemon/CUDA observer.
Experimental-profile capability selector and bounded memory probes.
cases.acceptance: Clients obey the configured tested caps, share only the intended allocation, and leave zero orphan daemon after final release; throughput guarantees remain explicitly unclaimed.

cases.title: Migrate static MIG nodes to DRA dynamic ownership deliberately
given: A node has administrator-created MIG partitions and at least one live consumer; target configuration enables DynamicMIG.
Ampere and Hopper+ variants are capability-selected separately.
fault_schedule: Attempt application-level migration with active partitions.
After explicit drain/release, enable the prepared dynamic profile and verify its startup behavior.
Attempt legacy Videoflow mix or manual geometry mutation through the application adapter while DRA owns the node.
assertions: Application deployment cannot implicitly enable DynamicMIG over live or preserved static partitions.
Migration records that the driver may destroy pre-existing foreign partitions; ownership transfer requires confirmed quiescence.
Ampere prerequisites are checked before startup; Hopper on-demand behavior is not assumed on Ampere.
Legacy geometry hooks are blocked on DRA-owned nodes.
evidence: Migration/admission decision and workload drain/release evidence.
NVML geometry before/after and allocator ownership record.
adapter_requirements: Explicit cluster-administration migration path distinct from application deploy.
GPU family capability detection and live-user drain barrier.
cases.acceptance: Active static users are never destroyed by an application deploy; post-drain transfer produces exactly one allocator owner and valid verified dynamic geometry.

cases.title: Do not deadlock GPU rollout when all allocatable devices are in use
given: One worker holds the only GPU or matching slice; a new image/config requires a replacement.
Rollout policy declares either reserved surge capacity or permitted drain/unavailability.
fault_schedule: Initiate update with no spare device, then delay the old worker's drain/release.
Repeat with real reserved spare capacity and with controller restart during replacement.
assertions: No-spare rollout uses the declared interruption/drain path or rejects an impossible availability requirement before proceeding.
Replacement does not wait forever behind an old worker that policy forbids removing.
Allocation is released only after drain and preparation/readiness precedes declaring the replacement available.
evidence: Deployment strategy, Pod/claim/device lifecycle timeline.
Drain/release and replacement readiness events.
adapter_requirements: Allocation-aware rollout policy and drain hook.
Real scheduler with bounded configurable rollout deadline.
cases.acceptance: The no-spare scenario either completes the permitted drained replacement within its configured deadline or rejects the incompatible availability requirement; it does not silently stall.

cases.title: Bound replica admission by actual GPU profiles and ancillary resources
given: Initial replica demand consumes all matching whole GPUs or MIG slices; optional scale-out asks for additional replicas.
A variant has spare GPUs but insufficient CPU/host memory or an incompatible GPU model/topology.
fault_schedule: Request scale-out while holding existing allocations.
Add compatible capacity and refresh the inventory; for managed-MIG geometry, require a separate safe allocation operation rather than assuming an extra slice exists.
assertions: Desired replicas, admitted replicas and ready replicas are distinct reported values.
Scale decisions are constrained by matching profile, per-host fit and declared ancillary resources.
No GPU count increase is reported as delivered processing capacity until allocation/preparation/readiness completes.
evidence: Capacity snapshot and per-replica admission/claim/pod conditions.
CPU/memory/resource requests and unavailable-capacity reason.
adapter_requirements: Allocation admission separate from autoscaler replica intent.
Resource requirements passed through all deployment backends.
cases.acceptance: Excess or incompatible replicas remain explicitly unadmitted/pending with a reason, and become admitted only after matching real capacity is observed.

cases.title: Preserve explicit hardware and locality requirements across backends
given: A request specifies GPU family/minimum memory, two devices on one host, and a required interconnect/NUMA locality when the selected backend can verify it.
Mixed eligible nodes include devices that satisfy count but not model/memory/topology.
fault_schedule: Apply through each selected backend and inspect actual allocation.
Remove or contradict required topology evidence in the inventory.
assertions: Count alone does not satisfy a stronger hardware requirement.
Backends either enforce requested constraints using validated attributes or reject the unsupported constraint explicitly.
Unspecified performance attributes are not upgraded into guarantees; optional preferences remain distinguishable from hard requirements.
evidence: Backend-neutral request, rendered constraints and allocated physical UUID/topology observations.
Capability rejection for unsupported hard constraints.
adapter_requirements: Independent hardware topology observer and per-backend constraint translation.
cases.acceptance: Every successful allocation satisfies all verifiable hard requirements; unsupported or unverifiable requirements fail explicitly instead of being dropped.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Qualify memory-fitting MIG profiles with measured workload budgets
given: A representative user-supplied workload has fixed input size, concurrency, processing rate target, maximum frame age and measured warmup/steady-state peak memory.
Candidate profiles all satisfy declared memory but have different compute/media-engine/bandwidth capacities.
fault_schedule: Run the same workload on candidate profiles under controlled shared-device load.
Include startup and peak batch phases; record transfer time and queue delay separately from inference.
Repeat after changing only the profile to identify whether compute, media engine or transfer limits matter.
assertions: A profile is qualified only against the workload's declared thresholds; smallest memory fit is not automatically deemed adequate.
Reports include delivered rate, latency/age distribution, drop count and peak memory alongside requested budget.
Unsupported media-engine or compute requirements are identified rather than hidden by a memory-only fit.
evidence: Versioned workload configuration, raw timing/memory traces and resource profile inventory.
Threshold comparison and confidence/repeatability information.
adapter_requirements: Independent benchmark runner; targets are inputs from the user/workload, never invented FPS numbers.
Candidate allocation selection and actual hardware profile observer.
cases.acceptance: Qualification requires meeting every supplied threshold over the defined trial; absent workload targets produce measurements only, not a scalability guarantee.

cases.title: Recover MIG ownership and original-state records across every lifecycle crash boundary
given: An operation records original configuration, claims ownership, publishes a generated entry, changes desired geometry and later restores it.
Original label is tested as absent, explicitly empty and a legitimate administrator value.
fault_schedule: Crash a fresh process after each persistent boundary in prepare and cleanup, then resume with no in-memory state.
Repeat restore after prior success and after a failed attempt; reorder duplicate API notifications.
Attempt a different operation with the same human flow name but a new allocation epoch.
assertions: Original state is recorded once with key-presence semantics and cannot be overwritten by a generated value.
Orphan claims/configuration entries are discoverable and reclaimable without touching another epoch.
Cleanup is idempotent; already-completed restoration does not trigger new unsafe reconfiguration.
Same human flow names do not conflate distinct active allocation lifetimes.
evidence: Boundary-by-boundary persisted records and API mutation journal.
Final original-state comparison plus orphan-owner/entry count.
adapter_requirements: Durable operation/epoch records and fresh-process recovery harness.
Deterministic crash barriers around real API writes; previously fixed annotation-presence behavior retained as regression coverage.
cases.acceptance: Every crash point converges to the intended active or fully restored state with no lost original value, no orphan records and no mutation of another epoch.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Resolve GPU count and memory defaults with explicit provenance
given: Fixtures cover no GPU declaration, default count=1, explicit count=1, explicit count=2, explicit memory demand, descriptor memory default and descriptor count default.
CPU variants distinguish inherited GPU defaults from explicitly supplied GPU-only requirements.
fault_schedule: Compile the same component under each backend with explicit-count/descriptor-memory and explicit-memory/descriptor-count combinations.
Round-trip the resolved requirement through serialization and local worker construction; change backend without changing the user declaration.
assertions: Default count=1 is not treated as an explicit demand for a whole device that cancels a memory-based slice request.
An explicit count override does not silently combine with an incompatible inherited memory default; chosen precedence is documented and any rejection names the descriptor as the source.
Two incompatible explicit requirements fail before launch; CPU handling does not silently drop an explicit GPU request.
A memory requirement mapped to a local whole GPU is checked against actual available memory, and delivered count is distinct from requested/default count.
evidence: Table of original value, source (explicit/descriptor/default), resolved requirement and backend decision.
Round-trip specification and local worker grant report.
adapter_requirements: Shared conformance table across backends; hardware memory verification delegated to the GPU admission cases.
cases.acceptance: Every table row has one documented deterministic result with accurate provenance; defaults never accidentally defeat an explicit requirement and incompatible explicit requests launch no worker.

cases.title: Superseding a buffered join delivery does not terminate its logical input
given: Two required parents A and B join by stable member identity; A is buffered and B is withheld.
The delivery adapter can redeliver the same logical A with a new attempt handle.
fault_schedule: Deliver A attempt1; expire its delivery lease and deliver A attempt2 while B remains absent.
Replace the worker before B arrives; then deliver B and allow recovery.
assertions: Replacing an attempt handle emits no terminal logical-input outcome.
The replacement can recover both members or their persisted group decision.
The complete group has one committed result; transport retries may occur.
evidence: Attempt-handle operation trace with logical and delivery identities.
Persisted group ledger and final sink member set.
adapter_requirements: Opaque delivery-attempt handles must be distinct from logical input identities.
Runtime owns handle replacement; messaging exposes acknowledge, retry and terminal semantics without implementing joins.
cases.acceptance: After the scheduled crash, A+B reaches a committed terminal outcome and no superseded attempt terminally removes A before that outcome.

cases.title: Join commit survives every partial input-acknowledgment crash boundary
given: A+B form a deterministic group; working retention can reclaim independently acknowledged inputs.
Durable group state and an output sink are instrumented by logical identity.
fault_schedule: Enumerate crashes before group persistence, after persistence, after output commitment, after ACK A, and before/after ACK B.
Restart from a fresh process with the same logical run and deliver remaining inputs.
assertions: No recovery path waits forever for an already reclaimed member.
Committed output and remaining input resolutions agree with one durable group decision.
Recomputation, if allowed before commitment, does not produce a second logical committed result.
evidence: Crash-point log and durable state snapshots for each boundary.
Output identities and acknowledgment trace after recovery.
adapter_requirements: Runtime requires a durable group ledger or state/outbox store separate from messaging and accelerator allocation.
Messaging provides stable member identity and recoverable deliveries; no assumption that several acknowledgments are atomic.
cases.acceptance: Every enumerated boundary terminates with exactly one committed logical group result and all member outcomes accounted for within the configured recovery deadline.

cases.title: State transition and ambiguous output publication recover from an outbox
given: A stateful accumulator updates state and publishes a derived event per group.
The sink records stable output identity; publication acknowledgments can be intercepted.
fault_schedule: Crash after state commit but before send.
In another run accept publication but lose its acknowledgment, then crash and replay the outbox.
assertions: State and output cannot permanently diverge.
Retry uses the original output identity and committed payload.
No second state transition occurs for the same committed group.
evidence: State revision history, outbox lifecycle and sink identity ledger.
Transport send/receipt/acknowledgment timeline.
adapter_requirements: State/outbox transaction belongs to runtime; messaging returns explicit accepted, rejected or ambiguous publication outcomes.
Allocator interfaces are not consulted by group commit.
cases.acceptance: All committed state transitions have a corresponding eventually resolved output; replay introduces no duplicate logical state transition.

cases.title: Nondeterministic inference has an explicit committed-result replay policy
given: A deliberately stochastic component returns a different nonce on each invocation.
The reliable profile declares that a committed result must be replayed byte-for-byte.
fault_schedule: Compute and persist a result, crash before all input acknowledgments, then restart.
Run a separate crash before result commitment to exercise allowed recomputation.
assertions: Once committed, recovery republishes the stored result and identity instead of silently recomputing it.
Precommit recomputation is distinguishable from replay in lineage.
A backend lacking the required durable result store is rejected before execution.
evidence: Invocation nonces, committed result hash and output lineage.
Capability-validation diagnostic for unsupported configuration.
adapter_requirements: Component declares determinism and replay policy; runtime persists results when required.
Messaging cannot infer determinism from its duplicate-suppression capability.
cases.acceptance: The committed payload hash is invariant across recovery; an unsupported replay guarantee fails admission without publishing data.

cases.title: Adversarial parent ordering cannot deadlock join credits
given: Two parent channels contain the same finite set of trace IDs in opposing orders.
Consumer credits and join capacity are deliberately smaller than the trace set; input data remains recoverable.
fault_schedule: Deliver early A halves and disjoint early B halves until both channels exhaust delivery credit.
Continue heartbeats and leave the network healthy; do not inject new inputs.
assertions: The runtime has a defined spill, admission, reordering or rejection strategy rather than renewing an impossible wait forever.
Completed groups preserve declared parent ordering.
The test distinguishes stalled matching from broker outage.
evidence: Per-parent credits, buffered member IDs, group progress and spill/admission decisions.
Watchdog outcome and complete expected group set when the declared configuration is supported.
adapter_requirements: Runtime negotiates minimum join working set or durable spill independently of the broker implementation.
Messaging exposes credit pressure and recoverable deferral without fabricating application progress.
cases.acceptance: The finite workload either completes every expected group or is rejected before execution with a specific working-set incompatibility; indefinite healthy-network stagnation fails.

cases.title: A permanently missing join branch follows a declared outcome
given: A join has a configured maximum wait and a declared missing-member policy: fail, drop or partial result.
A control fixture verifies that deliberately unbounded WAIT is explicitly declared and cancellable.
fault_schedule: Deliver A for trace1 and never produce B for trace1.
Advance a controllable clock past the configured wait; subsequently send cancellation to the unbounded-WAIT control.
assertions: The configured bounded policy resolves trace1 once and reports its missing member.
WAIT mode reports waiting rather than healthy processing progress.
Cancellation interrupts WAIT and releases or durably transfers ownership.
evidence: Clock transitions, join outcome record and worker completion status.
Delivery ownership trace after timeout or cancellation.
adapter_requirements: Join policy and timeout ownership belong to runtime, not accelerator allocation.
Messaging must support cancellation or abandonment of outstanding receives.
cases.acceptance: Bounded joins resolve by their configured deadline plus declared scheduler tolerance; explicitly unbounded joins remain observable and cancellable.

cases.title: Completion waits for every expected replica and its final sequence
given: One logical parent has two fixed replicas and a known membership epoch.
Replica1 has a delayed final output; downstream knows each replica final sequence convention.
fault_schedule: Replica0 publishes its final sequence and EOS.
Pause replica1 longer than the historical 500ms quiescence, then publish its final output and EOS.
assertions: Downstream cannot complete after only replica0 EOS or an empty observation interval.
Every required output through both final sequences is accounted for before successful completion.
Slow completion is not mistaken for failure or missing membership.
evidence: Replica membership, final-sequence records and downstream terminal timestamp.
Sink output identities relative to both EOS records.
adapter_requirements: Runtime owns completion barriers keyed by logical node, partition and epoch.
Messaging carries independently identifiable completion records and delivery observations; accelerator leases do not imply completion.
cases.acceptance: Successful downstream completion occurs only after both final-sequence obligations are resolved, including the deliberately delayed output.

cases.title: Duplicate and stale-epoch EOS cannot finish a replacement execution
given: A partition is replaced under a new execution epoch; its earlier EOS can be redelivered.
The new epoch has unfinished required output.
fault_schedule: Deliver duplicate old EOS after replacement starts.
Deliver new-epoch data, duplicate new EOS, and finally the new final-sequence obligation.
assertions: Old EOS is fenced to its recorded membership epoch.
Duplicates cannot increment a completion count twice.
The current epoch finishes once after its own obligations.
evidence: Epoch registry, accepted/rejected completion identities and barrier state transitions.
adapter_requirements: Runtime supplies epoch-aware membership and idempotent barrier updates.
Messaging preserves control-record identity without deciding whether an epoch is current.
cases.acceptance: Neither stale nor duplicate EOS can produce early success; exactly one current-epoch terminal decision is recorded.

cases.title: Unknown delivery state cannot satisfy a completion barrier
given: A parent EOS exists but at least one required input or output remains unresolved.
Broker state queries are observable and independently faultable from data delivery.
fault_schedule: Return timeouts and authorization errors from delivery-state queries during the drain check.
Restore query access and finish the outstanding work.
assertions: An unavailable query produces unknown state rather than zero pending work.
The runtime waits or fails explicitly during uncertainty.
Restored observations permit normal completion only after required work resolves.
evidence: Injected query errors, runtime completion-state transitions and final work ledger.
adapter_requirements: Messaging observations distinguish known-empty, known-pending and unavailable.
Runtime must not interpret a missing metric as a semantic completion guarantee.
cases.acceptance: No successful completion is recorded while the only evidence of emptiness is a failed query.

cases.title: ABORT remains distinct from normal end of stream across replicas
given: Two replicas feed a downstream join and one will fail terminally.
The sink records terminal status independently of delivered data.
fault_schedule: Publish normal EOS from one replica and terminal ABORT from the other in both orders.
Repeat ABORT, then restart a downstream process before it records terminal status.
assertions: ABORT cannot be hidden by an already observed EOS.
The final logical run is failed or explicitly partial according to its declared contract, never silently successful.
Recovery preserves the terminal cause and does not fabricate missing results.
evidence: Terminal cause lineage, completion state and remaining work disposition.
adapter_requirements: Runtime defines terminal-status precedence and propagation.
Messaging represents control types separately; allocator cleanup follows runtime termination rather than manufacturing it.
cases.acceptance: All orderings and restarts retain the declared failure outcome and its cause; no case becomes success merely because EOS arrived first.

cases.title: Independent watchdog detects a hung callback despite healthy heartbeats
given: A worker receives an input and its process callback blocks on a controllable latch indefinitely.
The I/O loop and delivery-heartbeat task stay responsive; processing deadline D is configured.
fault_schedule: Block the callback after entering inference while allowing normal heartbeats.
Advance past D plus the declared watchdog scheduling tolerance.
assertions: The watchdog runs independently of callback return and records a stalled-computation diagnosis.
Worker replacement or configured terminal handling begins by the deadline.
Outstanding input ownership remains recoverable according to the selected reliable profile.
evidence: Callback entry, heartbeat timestamps, watchdog event and worker lifecycle trace.
adapter_requirements: Runtime owns progress supervision and cancellation; messaging lease heartbeats are liveness signals only.
Component declares expected deadline or progress hooks.
cases.acceptance: A callback that never returns is diagnosed by D plus declared tolerance even though broker heartbeats continue.

cases.title: Legitimate slow inference and idle sources do not trigger false progress failures
given: One component has a declared long startup/warmup and processing deadline; another waits with no outstanding work.
A deterministic clock and explicit component progress events are available.
fault_schedule: Warm up and run slow inference inside its declared budget; hold the idle source silent longer than that budget.
Then withhold declared progress after a known work item starts.
assertions: Startup, idle waiting and active processing are distinct runtime states.
No false restart occurs for allowed warmup or absence of work.
A real processing stall is still detected after the declared deadline.
evidence: State-machine trace, configured deadlines, progress events and restart count.
adapter_requirements: Component supplies meaningful startup and work progress semantics.
Runtime evaluates those semantics independently of messaging throughput or accelerator occupancy.
cases.acceptance: Control runs complete with zero false restarts, while the injected active-work stall triggers the configured recovery action.

cases.title: Timed-out output publication has one authoritative owner
given: Output capacity can block a worker publication while input recovery remains enabled.
The runtime publication operation has explicit cancellation, ambiguous-result and retry states.
fault_schedule: Block publication until the synchronous caller times out.
Release capacity after the input has been marked for retry; also test lost publication acknowledgment after actual acceptance.
assertions: An orphaned background coroutine cannot publish a second differently identified result after the runtime relinquishes ownership.
The accepted-versus-unknown case is reconciled through the same output identity.
Cancellation or reconciliation is durably visible before starting a competing attempt.
evidence: Operation IDs, publication acceptance/timeout/cancellation log and input attempt transitions.
adapter_requirements: Messaging exposes publication operation identity and ambiguity rather than hiding a continuing retry task.
Runtime owns the attempt/outbox lifecycle; cancellation does not pretend a remote acceptance can be undone.
cases.acceptance: Each logical output has one reconciled final outcome and no unowned task can create a conflicting result after timeout.

cases.title: Live-source restarts create new epochs without colliding with earlier frames
given: A live source has no replayable persistent frame offset and uses a stable run ID.
The broker duplicate window covers the planned restart interval.
fault_schedule: Emit frames with source-local sequence0..4; crash and restart the source within the window.
Emit five genuinely new frames from local sequence0 again.
assertions: New physical frames have new logical source-epoch identities.
Earlier retry attempts preserve their old identity rather than masquerading as new captures.
All ten intended frames are distinguishable in lineage and downstream acceptance.
evidence: Source epoch allocation, capture payload hashes and message/output identity ledger.
adapter_requirements: Runtime/source adapter owns capture epochs and stable source offsets.
Messaging duplicate suppression consumes supplied identity; accelerator allocation is irrelevant.
cases.acceptance: No genuinely new post-restart frame is suppressed because its local counter matches a pre-restart frame.

cases.title: Replayable sources preserve stable offset identities across attempts
given: A finite source has durable media identity and frame offsets; the same offsets can be replayed.
The run policy distinguishes recovery replay from an intentionally new analysis version.
fault_schedule: Crash after publishing an offset but before source checkpoint confirmation; restart and replay it.
Execute a separate new analysis version over the same media.
assertions: Recovery replay keeps the original logical input identity.
An intentionally new analysis has a declared analysis/version namespace rather than accidentally colliding with old output.
Checkpoint progress never skips an offset due to an ambiguous send.
evidence: Media/version/offset identity map and source checkpoint history.
adapter_requirements: Source checkpoint and identity policy belongs to runtime/source adapters.
Messaging accepts deterministic IDs and reports publication ambiguity.
cases.acceptance: Recovered offsets map one-to-one to original logical identities; new-analysis identities follow the declared namespace and no offset is silently lost.

cases.title: Distinct time-aligned groups cannot collide after timestamp rounding
given: Construct two time-join groups with different member identities and distinct times rounding to the same microsecond.
Use exactly representable fixture values and include a replay of the first member set.
fault_schedule: Assemble both groups in each parent-arrival order, then reassemble the first group after simulated recovery.
assertions: Distinct member sets have distinct group IDs even when rounded timestamps agree.
Replaying the same member set retains its group ID.
Group identity includes the necessary source/epoch/window namespace.
evidence: Member-set-to-group-ID table and deterministic collision regression fixture.
adapter_requirements: Runtime defines canonical group identity from stable members and window identity.
Messaging transports IDs and cannot repair application-level collisions.
cases.acceptance: No collision occurs for the adversarial member sets, and replay of an identical set is identity-stable.

cases.title: Sink side effects and idempotency markers survive crash and concurrent replay
given: A sink fixture exposes an externally observable counter and optional atomic idempotency-key API.
The component declares either idempotent effects or only at-least-once side effects.
fault_schedule: Crash after applying the effect but before writing the runtime marker.
Race two deliveries through the seen-then-consume window; also restart after marker persistence.
Replay after the marker/idempotency retention horizon, including the reviewed 86400-second default as an accelerated configured-window variant; test concurrent replay across expiry.
assertions: An idempotent sink uses the external system transaction/idempotency primitive so one logical effect occurs.
A plain side-effect sink is never certified exactly once by a separate Redis marker.
The declared weaker guarantee is visible in admission/result metadata.
Effect-idempotency retention covers the admitted recovery/replay horizon; a request beyond it is explicitly rejected or declares possible duplicate effects, never certified exactly once.
evidence: External effect ledger, idempotency keys, runtime marker history and concurrent attempt trace.
Configured effect-key retention versus replay horizon and effect count after expiration.
adapter_requirements: Component owns side-effect atomicity with the external service; runtime supplies stable effect identity.
Messaging and accelerator backends cannot upgrade a nontransactional external effect to exactly once.
cases.acceptance: Idempotent mode produces one external effect for all schedules; unsupported stronger guarantees are rejected rather than inferred from a local marker.

cases.title: Singleton joins cannot become competing multiworker joins through autoscaling
given: A singleton two-parent join is rendered with autoscaling requested; test both trace and time joins.
A test scheduler can steer matching A and B halves to different pods if scaling is admitted.
fault_schedule: Request scale1-to2 and attempt the split-half delivery schedule.
assertions: Unsupported elastic joins are rejected before a second competing worker starts.
If elastic joins are implemented, stable group routing sends both halves to one fenced owner.
Static constructor nb_tasks cannot bypass runtime eligibility checks.
evidence: Admission decision, rendered target, actual pod membership and member ownership trace.
adapter_requirements: Runtime declares join/state scaling capability; deployment consults it independently of backend choice.
Messaging provides routing primitives only after a valid ownership plan exists.
cases.acceptance: The split-half schedule either cannot be admitted or completes every group under a verified ownership protocol; waiting forever is failure.

cases.title: Partition intent survives a singleton-to-multiple-worker scale request
given: A tracker declares partition_by=camera_id with initial replica count1.
Frames from the same camera carry consecutive sequence numbers and update visible state.
fault_schedule: Request scale1-to3 while continuing one camera stream.
Exercise restart and scale-down paths as well.
assertions: Partition/state declaration is not erased by initial replica count1.
Without ownership migration support, scale is blocked before replicas diverge.
With support, one fenced owner processes each key and state follows ownership.
evidence: Compiled intent versus runtime membership, per-camera state revisions and scale decision.
adapter_requirements: Runtime preserves partition intent separately from deployment replica count.
Allocator provisions granted capacity only after runtime authorizes scaling.
cases.acceptance: One camera history is never split among independent unfenced states; unsupported singleton expansion fails explicitly.

cases.title: Missing and malformed partition keys follow an explicit policy
given: A component requires a string camera_id; include valid keys, absent keys, null, empty strings and wrong types.
The policy for invalid keys is declared as reject or a named fallback partition.
fault_schedule: Interleave invalid records with valid camera histories under several replicas.
Retry invalid records and restart one owner.
assertions: Invalid keys are not silently hashed as the string None.
Rejected records have a traceable terminal/retry outcome; a declared fallback is observable and bounded.
Valid keys retain stable ownership and unaffected state.
evidence: Validation diagnostics, partition decisions and per-key processing ledger.
adapter_requirements: Component schema/runtime validates partition keys before routing or accelerator work.
Messaging must preserve typed metadata and return invalid-input diagnostics to runtime.
cases.acceptance: Every invalid-key fixture follows its declared policy and no implicit all-invalid hotspot is accepted as normal distribution.

cases.title: Camera state follows declared ordering under delayed and duplicate frames
given: A deterministic tracker fixture updates state from ordered camera sequence numbers.
The declared late-frame policy is reorder within a bounded horizon or explicitly drop/mark late data.
fault_schedule: Deliver sequences1,3,2,3 for cameraA while interleaving cameraB.
Delay sequence2 past the horizon in a second run and redeliver after a worker restart.
assertions: No arrival-order race silently changes the declared temporal semantics.
Duplicates do not apply state twice.
Late data is either incorporated in ordered processing or explicitly accounted for as late/drop.
evidence: Per-camera input, accepted-order and state-transition logs compared with a reference interpreter.
adapter_requirements: Runtime/component defines sequence, event-time and late-data semantics; broker delivery order is insufficient.
Accelerator placement must not determine state ownership or ordering.
cases.acceptance: Final state and late/drop outcomes match the declared reference policy for every delivery permutation.

cases.title: Stateful worker restart restores a consistent checkpoint and replay position
given: A keyed accumulator stores a durable checkpoint and records consumed member identities.
A stateless placement replacement may occur on a different process or host.
fault_schedule: Crash before checkpoint, after checkpoint, and after input acknowledgment boundaries.
Replace the worker and replay remaining recoverable inputs.
assertions: Checkpoint state and replay position describe the same committed prefix.
Recovered state equals the uninterrupted reference result.
An ephemeral-state-only component is not admitted under restart-safe stateful claims.
evidence: Checkpoint revision/offset pairs, restart trace and reference-state comparison.
adapter_requirements: Runtime/component state store is a distinct capability from message persistence and GPU allocation.
Deployment passes stable logical state identity to replacements.
cases.acceptance: Every crash boundary converges to the reference state or is rejected before execution as an unsupported recovery profile.

cases.title: State handoff fences old owners during scale and network partitions
given: A future elastic keyed runtime supports durable ownership epochs and checkpoint transfer.
Old ownerA is paused rather than killed so it can resume after ownerB starts.
fault_schedule: Transfer a key to B, deliver new records, then resume A with a buffered old input.
Partition A from the ownership service while leaving its output transport reachable.
assertions: Only the current ownership epoch can commit state/output.
B starts from the transferred committed prefix.
Old-owner attempts remain rejected even when their GPU lease or message connection still works.
evidence: Ownership epoch history, rejected stale commits and final state/output ledger.
adapter_requirements: Runtime supplies fencing and state migration; neither durable consumer names nor accelerator leases are ownership fences.
Unsupported elastic state must be rejected before scaling.
cases.acceptance: No stale owner commits after transfer, and the combined result matches a single-owner reference history.

cases.title: Worker concurrency reconciles stage-wide work credits
given: Twenty pending tasks feed ten independent one-at-a-time workers; each task blocks at a start barrier.
Host/payload byte budgets can hold ten in-flight tasks.
fault_schedule: Run the historical shared-consumer eight-credit configuration as a regression control.
Apply the declared ten-worker execution plan, then scale workers up and down.
assertions: The adapter exposes stage-wide credit semantics and runtime derives enough credits for admitted active concurrency.
All ten admitted workers can reach the task-start barrier before any task finishes.
Scale changes reconcile credits without exceeding configured memory budgets.
evidence: Broker pending/unacknowledged state, worker start-barrier count and credit configuration changes.
adapter_requirements: Messaging exposes consumer-wide credit limits generically; runtime calculates concurrency demand.
Allocator reports usable worker grants but does not configure message credits.
cases.acceptance: With ten admitted tasks of concurrency and sufficient explicit budget, ten workers start; the historical eight-credit control starts only eight and is detected as incompatible.

cases.title: Prefetch fairness and byte admission remain bounded under skewed workers
given: Workers have different simulated processing delays and input sizes alternate between small messages and 1MB frames.
A declared per-worker prefetch limit and aggregate resident-byte budget B are enforced.
fault_schedule: Start the slow worker first so it can capture credit, then start faster workers.
Pause the slow worker while continuing input until admission becomes limiting.
assertions: Prefetch cannot consume unbounded aggregate memory or permanently hoard all runnable work.
Faster workers receive eligible tasks when capacity exists.
Every blocked/dropped input has an explicit pressure outcome.
evidence: Per-worker queue bytes, aggregate resident payload bytes, assignment trace and pressure decisions.
adapter_requirements: Runtime owns byte admission and fairness policy; messaging provides bounded receive/pause and observable credits.
Allocator capacity alone cannot authorize unlimited prefetch.
cases.acceptance: Measured resident queue payload never exceeds B plus the documented atomic-admission tolerance; runnable capacity is not indefinitely starved by another worker prefetching.

cases.title: Live-video autoscaling observes overload that lossy retention conceals
given: A controllable source offers rate greater than measured one-worker processing capacity.
The lossy input path retains one latest message; required delivery/freshness objectives and control interval are declared.
fault_schedule: Sustain overload while conventional queue depth remains at or below the tiny retention limit.
Add allocatable capacity, then reduce offered load.
assertions: Autoscaling evaluates offered/processed rate, age or drop observations sufficient to detect the declared objective breach.
It requests only admissible stateless capacity and respects stabilization policy.
Missing metrics produce explicit unknown state, not healthy zero demand.
evidence: Offered/processed/drop counts, frame-age distribution, scaler inputs and replica decisions.
adapter_requirements: Runtime exports workload demand; deployment control combines it with accelerator-admission capacity.
Messaging queue depth is one observation, not the universal demand contract.
cases.acceptance: The configured objective breach is detected within its declared control window despite a shallow queue; no arbitrary FPS target is imposed by this test.

cases.title: Batch scaling targets a supported workload controller
given: A finite batch processor requests scaling and is rendered as a Job.
A Kubernetes test cluster has the selected autoscaling controller installed.
fault_schedule: Render, validate and apply the execution plan; create backlog sufficient to trigger its declared scaling rule.
Observe actual Job parallelism or explicitly fixed parallelism.
assertions: The scaler targets the real workload kind and an API supporting the requested scaling behavior.
Unsupported batch-autoscaling combinations fail before workload creation.
Batch completion accounts for all admitted task instances.
evidence: Rendered resources, API validation, controller events and actual workload concurrency.
adapter_requirements: Deployment adapter exposes supported controller/scaling capabilities.
Runtime defines batch completion independently of Kubernetes kind; allocator supplies capacity only.
cases.acceptance: A supported scaling plan changes actual batch concurrency and completes; otherwise admission rejects it before creating a dangling Deployment-targeted scaler.

cases.title: Autoscaling admission reconciles granted accelerator capacity
given: Initial execution plan has one granted worker and requested maximum ten; allocator fixture exposes only two matching allocations.
A no-spare-capacity variant exposes one allocation.
fault_schedule: Drive workload demand above one-worker capacity.
Withdraw and later restore one allocation while scale requests are pending.
assertions: Desired runtime concurrency is distinguished from granted schedulable concurrency.
The runtime never treats Pending pods or an allocator request as ready processing capacity.
Bounded waiting, rejection or partial admission is explicit and reconciles when capacity changes.
evidence: Demand decisions, allocation request/response IDs, readiness and actual worker count.
adapter_requirements: Allocator returns admitted quantity/capability and lifecycle status; deployment consumes that result through an interface.
No messaging adapter performs GPU geometry changes as a side effect of lag.
cases.acceptance: Active concurrency never exceeds valid grants and the no-spare case reports a capacity constraint rather than silently claiming successful scale-out.

cases.title: Exact-capacity GPU rollout uses an explicit feasible upgrade policy
given: A running singleton consumes the only matching accelerator allocation.
Two permitted policies are tested: drain-and-replace with allowed interruption, or reserve spare upgrade capacity.
fault_schedule: Change the worker image digest and apply the rollout with no unadvertised spare device.
Repeat with two and three fully allocated replicas.
assertions: The selected policy does not inherit an infeasible zero-unavailable plus positive-surge requirement.
Drain-and-replace releases the old grant before replacement scheduling.
A zero-interruption policy rejects missing reserved capacity before initiating an impossible upgrade.
evidence: Deployment strategy, pod/grant lifecycle and rollout completion or admission diagnostic.
adapter_requirements: Deployment owns upgrade policy and readiness/drain orchestration; allocator exposes release and replacement capacity.
Messaging is informed of quiescence but does not choose rollout availability guarantees.
cases.acceptance: The image update completes under its admitted availability policy or is rejected for insufficient spare capacity; indefinite Pending replacement is failure.

cases.title: GPU scale-down and rollout drain outstanding work before releasing grants
given: A worker has one active inference and prefetched recoverable inputs.
Its replacement can start after the old allocation is safely released.
fault_schedule: Request scale-down or image rollout while inference is paused.
Exercise graceful completion and forced deadline expiry branches.
assertions: New input admission stops before drain begins.
Graceful outputs commit before release; forced termination leaves unresolved work recoverable under the selected profile.
No process continues accelerator work after its grant is reassigned.
evidence: Quiesce, active work, output commit, delivery ownership and grant-release timestamps.
adapter_requirements: Runtime exposes quiesce/drain/abort; messaging exposes stop-receive and recovery; allocator exposes release confirmation.
Deployment sequences all three interfaces without treating process exit as successful application completion.
cases.acceptance: No admitted input disappears and no old/new processes concurrently use the same exclusive grant after reassignment; forced drains have explicit failure/retry outcomes.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Host CPU and RAM requests participate in GPU worker admission
given: Model fixtures declare measurable CPU demand, startup RAM and steady-state host buffers.
A test node has sufficient GPU capacity but insufficient RAM for all requested replicas.
fault_schedule: Render and schedule the workload, then exercise simultaneous model startup and maximum declared input buffers.
assertions: CPU/RAM requests and configured limits are preserved from workload contract through pod admission.
The scheduler cannot admit all replicas solely because GPU resources fit.
Measured startup/buffer peaks are checked against the declared host budget rather than GPU memory declarations.
evidence: Rendered resource fields, scheduler decisions and process RSS/CPU measurements.
adapter_requirements: Component supplies host resource requirements; deployment adapter preserves them; allocator must not conflate host memory with VRAM.
Messaging exposes resident payload accounting needed by runtime admission.
cases.acceptance: The resource-insufficient plan is rejected or remains explicitly unadmitted, and admitted startup stays within the declared resource policy without relying on unconfigured namespace defaults.

cases.title: Model compatibility and locality requirements constrain placement
given: Two GPU nodes advertise different model capabilities; only one satisfies a fixture requirement such as compute capability or media-engine support.
A separate locality constraint requires a specific data zone or colocated execution group.
fault_schedule: Make the compatible/local node unavailable while keeping generic GPU count sufficient.
Restore it and launch the same plan.
assertions: Hard capability/locality requirements are not silently downgraded to generic GPU pool membership.
The incompatible placement is rejected or waits explicitly.
When admitted, startup verifies the actual capability before serving work.
evidence: Requirement schema, placement decision, node identity and runtime capability report.
adapter_requirements: Component declares requirements; allocator/deployment selects matching resources; runtime validates delivery.
Messaging backend selection does not determine model compatibility.
cases.acceptance: No fixture executes on an incompatible or prohibited host; successful admission demonstrates the declared capability on the actual runtime resource.
cases.qualification_notes: The primary fixture can establish API/lifecycle invariants. Any physical device preparation, restoration, visibility or topology assertion also requires a real-GPU variant; mocks do not qualify that claim.

cases.title: Worker relocation preserves model and input asset identity
given: A model or media file exists on hostA only; hostB has either no file or different bytes at the same path.
The asset contract includes expected content identity and local-only versus portable storage semantics.
fault_schedule: Start on A, evict the pod, and attempt rescheduling on B.
Repeat using a declared portable artifact source.
assertions: HostPath is not treated as evidence that the same asset exists everywhere.
Local-only assets constrain placement or fail explicitly after relocation.
Portable assets are verified by identity before readiness and processing.
evidence: Asset digests, mounts/download records, node assignment and readiness diagnostics.
adapter_requirements: Deployment/artifact provider owns distribution; component declares asset identity; runtime verifies it.
Neither messaging persistence nor an accelerator grant implies model-file availability.
cases.acceptance: Relocation never processes with silently missing or changed model/input bytes; the portable variant resumes with the verified asset.

cases.title: Nonowner replicas route from metadata without downloading image bodies
given: A fixed partitioned stage has four then eight replicas and 1MB payload references.
Instrument body reads per replica and keep key metadata available without hydration.
fault_schedule: Deliver a finite unique-frame set across all partitions; no retries or body-store faults occur.
Pause a nonowner replica and repeat the workload.
assertions: Only the owner hydrates each body for this single-consumer execution contract.
Nonowner routing does not require image decoding or accelerator allocation.
Exactly one owner processes each frame and reader-lifecycle bookkeeping remains consistent.
evidence: Per-frame owner map, body-read count/bytes by replica and output identities.
adapter_requirements: Messaging envelope parsing exposes routing metadata separately from body loading.
Runtime ownership is resolved before the payload adapter fetch; allocator receives no routing responsibility.
cases.acceptance: With no retries and one intended processing reader, each frame has one hydration regardless of replica count; duplicate full-body fetches by nonowners fail.

cases.title: Fused GPU execution groups preserve semantics and remove internal transfers
given: A deterministic decode/transform/inference chain has a reference unfused result and an explicitly supported fused execution-group declaration.
Instrumentation records host-device copies and network payload bytes at each boundary.
fault_schedule: Run identical finite frames through unfused and fused variants.
Crash the fused worker between internal stages and exercise the declared retry boundary.
For the separately advertised gpu_resident_edges variant, choose compatible stages with declared expected host-device/device-device copy budgets and record actual transfers between them.
assertions: Fused and unfused results agree within model-declared numeric tolerance and preserve lineage.
Internal fused edges do not serialize full frames through the messaging adapter.
Recovery uses the declared group boundary and does not claim independent commits for invisible internal edges.

A GPU-resident-edge claim meets its explicitly declared transfer budget on compatible internal edges; zero broker traffic alone cannot qualify device residency. Ordinary process fusion is a weaker separate capability.
evidence: Result comparison, copy/transfer trace and retry-boundary log.
adapter_requirements: Component/execution-group abstraction owns fusion and device residency; messaging handles only declared external edges.
Allocator grants resources to the group without implementing graph semantics.
cases.acceptance: A supported fused path matches the reference semantics and has zero broker body transfers on declared internal edges; unsupported fusion must fail compilation before deployment.
cases.capability_scope: gpu_fusion; gpu_resident_edges is a separate variant

cases.title: Cross-camera dynamic batching respects latency, identity and fairness contracts
given: A batching component declares maximum batch size, maximum wait D and per-camera fairness policy.
One camera is busy and another emits sparse frames; a partial batch remains at EOS.
fault_schedule: Feed skewed arrivals, pause one camera, and send EOS before the batch fills.
Inject one invalid item and a worker cancellation during batch assembly.
assertions: Each valid input maps to its own result identity and declared error outcome.
A sparse input cannot wait beyond D plus measured scheduler tolerance solely for a fuller batch.
EOS flushes admitted partial work and cancellation has a defined disposition.
evidence: Batch membership, arrival/dispatch timestamps, per-camera wait distributions and output mapping.
adapter_requirements: Component/runtime batching policy is distinct from transport fetch batch size and accelerator allocation.
Messaging exposes inputs and cancellation; allocator reports capacity without promising automatic batching.
cases.acceptance: All admitted items are accounted for, maximum batching delay honors D plus declared tolerance, and the selected fairness policy holds without an invented throughput target.

cases.title: Tracktor model and tensors use compatible granted CUDA devices
given: Tracktor receives two actual visible CUDA devices with detector and re-ID placement instrumented.
Use representative detection boxes producing at least one re-ID crop.
fault_schedule: Exercise model initialization, crop creation, re-ID inference and subsequent cross-model tensor operations.
Repeat with a remapped two-device grant whose host ordinals are not0,1.
assertions: Every tensor entering re-ID is on its model device or explicitly transferred there.
Runtime logical device indices respect the delivered grant rather than host numbering.
Inference completes with finite outputs and no hidden CPU fallback.
evidence: Actual tensor/model device trace, granted device identities and CUDA execution trace.
adapter_requirements: Component owns model/tensor placement; allocator exposes the granted device set and topology.
A recording fake is a fast unit check but cannot substitute for this actual CUDA acceptance test.
