cases.acceptance: The full affected inference path executes successfully on the intended granted devices for both ordinary and remapped grants.

cases.title: TeamClassifier SigLIP executes on its declared backend
given: TeamClassifier requests GPU SigLIP execution; weights and image processor are instrumented.
A separate explicit CPU configuration is the control.
fault_schedule: Load the model and classify representative crops under the GPU grant.
Remove usable CUDA support in a negative fixture while keeping the declared GPU requirement.
assertions: GPU mode places both model and input tensors on the actual granted CUDA device.
Startup reports actual backend/device and rejects unmet hard GPU requirements.
Explicit CPU mode remains valid and requests no unnecessary accelerator.
evidence: Parameter/input device inspection, framework execution trace and startup capability report.
adapter_requirements: Component owns execution placement and fallback policy; allocator reservation is insufficient evidence of GPU use.
Runtime readiness requires verification of the component-declared backend.
cases.acceptance: GPU mode demonstrably executes the affected model on CUDA; the unmet-requirement fixture fails before readiness rather than reserving an idle GPU while using CPU.

cases.title: Runtime grant enumeration accepts ordinal and UUID device masks
given: The allocation adapter supplies valid grants expressed as ordinals, physical GPU UUIDs and supported MIG UUIDs.
A CUDA runtime query independently reports the actual visible logical devices.
fault_schedule: Initialize a worker under each supported mask and query granted_gpus plus actual runtime devices.
Include an explicit empty grant and an invalid token as negative controls.
assertions: Valid UUID masks do not become an empty grant merely because they are not integers.
Logical CUDA indices and persistent physical identities are distinct and mapped correctly.
Unsupported masks fail explicitly; CPU fallback follows declared policy only.
evidence: Delivered grant, environment mask and CUDA enumeration comparison.
adapter_requirements: Allocator delivers stable device identities and runtime-visible handles; component/runtime validates visibility without parsing only host ordinals.
Driver-specific grant creation remains allocator-adapter responsibility.
cases.acceptance: For every supported grant form the reported logical device set equals CUDA visibility; invalid or empty grants cannot be misreported as a valid requested multi-device allocation.

cases.title: Shared TensorFlow workers honor declared peak-memory admission
given: Two compatible TensorFlow component fixtures share one device under an explicitly nonisolated sharing policy.
Measured startup/warmup/steady-state memory envelopes and configured growth/caps are recorded.
fault_schedule: Start both processes concurrently, warm both models and exercise maximum declared batch/buffer sizes.
Repeat with deliberately overcommitted declared demand.
assertions: Session configuration follows the selected coexistence policy rather than greedily reserving an undeclared device-sized pool.
Actual peaks are included in admission evidence; model weights alone are not used as the bound.
Overcommit is rejected or reported as unsupported before both workers are declared ready.
evidence: Session memory configuration, per-process/device peak usage and startup readiness outcomes.
adapter_requirements: Component owns framework memory behavior and measured working set; allocator states isolation/sharing guarantees.
Runtime admission accounts for aggregate declared demand but does not pretend growth is hardware isolation.
cases.acceptance: Under strict aggregate admission, the over-budget demand set is rejected before concurrent launch; the fitting fixture starts and processes within its declared memory envelope. Both cooperative-sharing fixtures explicitly report lack of hard isolation; advisory mode never certifies a strict admission guarantee.

cases.title: Pose GPU environment selects one ONNX Runtime distribution and verifies CUDA execution
given: Build clean CPU and GPU pose environments from declared packaging extras.
Inspect installed distributions and configure provider fallback policy explicitly.
fault_schedule: Initialize ONNX Runtime sessions and run representative inference on the GPU environment.
Run a negative fixture missing CUDA provider dependencies and a clean CPU control.
assertions: A deployment does not install competing onnxruntime and onnxruntime-gpu distributions that own the same import package.
GPU mode verifies selected providers and actual node execution rather than only package presence.
Missing hard-required CUDA support fails readiness instead of silently passing via CPU.

adapter_requirements: Component image/package contract owns runtime variants and provider requirements.
Allocator grants hardware; runtime/component verifies the software backend can use it.
cases.acceptance: Each environment has one intended ONNX Runtime distribution; GPU inference shows the declared provider behavior and the negative fixture is rejected before readiness.

cases.title: VLM automatic device mapping reports actual use and enforces offload policy
given: A VLM component receives a multi-device grant and declares whether CPU/disk offload is permitted.
Fixtures cover a model fitting one GPU and a model requiring a broader placement.
fault_schedule: Load with automatic device mapping, perform warmup and representative generation.
Constrain available memory so forbidden offload would otherwise be selected.
assertions: Actual module placement, device memory and CPU/disk offload are reported.
A grant of two devices is not certified as tensor parallelism or doubled throughput.
Forbidden offload fails admission/readiness; permitted offload is visible in the result configuration.

Messaging delivery mode cannot determine or claim model parallelism.
cases.acceptance: Observed placement obeys the declared offload policy and reports actual resource use; no throughput claim is derived solely from gpu_count.

cases.title: Multi-device workload validates topology rather than only a device count
given: A component explicitly requires a topology property such as peer access for its supported execution path.
Provide two-device fixtures with and without that property; include a count-only component as control.
fault_schedule: Initialize each component under both allocations and run a representative cross-device operation.
assertions: Hard topology requirements are verified before readiness.
A count-only grant cannot silently satisfy a stronger component requirement.
Components that do not require the property remain usable on the weaker topology.
evidence: Requirement/grant match, runtime peer/topology check and cross-device execution result.
adapter_requirements: Component declares actual parallel execution requirements; allocator describes topology capabilities; runtime verifies delivery.
Kubernetes resource count alone does not imply a model parallel implementation.
cases.acceptance: Compatible fixtures execute the required operation and incompatible fixtures fail before processing; no universal NVLink requirement is imposed on components that do not need it.

cases.title: Local undersupply and fallback preserve the component resource contract
given: A native or Python worker declares a hard two-device requirement; another declares optional GPU with CPU fallback.
The local adapter fixture exposes one GPU, zero GPUs and a container path without GPU injection.
fault_schedule: Launch each fixture and inspect delivered grant, startup device checks and readiness.
Repeat with oversubscribed cooperative sharing explicitly requested.
assertions: Hard two-device requirements fail when only one or zero usable devices are delivered.
Optional fallback is explicit and reported as CPU execution.
Local wraparound sharing is labeled nonexclusive and cannot inherit exclusive guarantees from deployment configuration.
evidence: Requested versus delivered grants, subprocess/container launch configuration and startup decisions.
adapter_requirements: Allocator/local execution adapter reports actual usable grants; component validates minimum resources and fallback policy.
Runtime cannot trust a requested gpu_count when the delivered environment differs.
cases.acceptance: No worker is declared ready under an unmet hard resource contract; explicit fallback/sharing succeeds only with accurate observed capability reporting.

cases.title: Tail-latency objectives cannot be inferred from count and sum alone
given: Two deterministic latency populations have the same count and sum:100 observations of10ms versus90 of1ms plus10 of91ms.
The declared nearest-rank p95 values are10ms and91ms; an objective threshold lies between them.
fault_schedule: Feed each population through the actual metric-export and objective-evaluation path.
Merge observations across two workers and restart one exporter to exercise interval and reset handling.
assertions: The observer distinguishes the two tail behaviors using supported histograms, sketches or retained samples.
A count/sum-only adapter reports percentile unavailable rather than labeling a mean as p95.
Aggregation and resets preserve the declared error bounds and observation window.
evidence: Exported metric samples, reference percentiles and objective decisions with estimator error bounds.
adapter_requirements: Runtime telemetry declares which distribution statistics it can support; deployment uses only supported demand/objective observations.
Messaging and accelerator metrics do not substitute for measured end-to-end frame latency.
cases.acceptance: The p95-capable path separates the two populations within its declared error bound; the count/sum-only path explicitly rejects a p95 decision rather than returning an invented estimate.

cases.title: Multi-input demand evaluation observes every required parent
given: A multi-input workload has a declared scaling eligibility contract and separately observable parent channels.
Fixtures distinguish a backed-up second parent from a missing first parent and from sufficient matched work with processing saturation.
fault_schedule: Hold the first parent lag constant while increasing second-parent backlog and oldest input age.
Swap declared parent order without changing the physical workload; then withhold one required branch entirely.
assertions: Demand diagnosis is invariant to arbitrary parent-list ordering.
The controller observes second-parent pressure and distinguishes missing-input stalls from processing capacity shortfall.
An unsupported elastic join remains blocked even when pressure exists; autoscaling cannot pretend extra workers repair a missing branch.
evidence: Per-parent demand/age observations, eligibility checks and invariant controller decisions across reordered graph declarations.
adapter_requirements: Runtime supplies multi-input workload semantics and eligibility; messaging supplies observations per logical subscription.
Deployment demand policy combines all required inputs instead of selecting the first backend channel.
cases.acceptance: Equivalent graphs with permuted parent declarations yield the same pressure diagnosis, and missing required input is not misclassified as a GPU capacity solution.

cases.title: Concurrent Kubernetes runs cannot overwrite another runs configuration or workload
given: Two executions use the same flow/node names and namespace but distinct run IDs and configuration/model digests.
The deployment contract either supports concurrent runs or explicitly enforces a single active run.
fault_schedule: Start runA and apply runB while A processes identifiable inputs.
Delete runB, restart an A pod and inspect the configuration it loads; include both Job and Deployment variants.
assertions: Concurrent mode gives run-owned configuration, workload and selectors noncolliding identities.
RunB cannot overwrite ConfigMaps, alter runA pod templates or trigger immutable-Job errors as its accidental concurrency mechanism.
Single-run mode rejects runB before mutating any A-owned resource; deleting B cannot delete or reconfigure A.
evidence: Kubernetes object UIDs/names/owners, resource diffs, pod configuration digests and per-run output ledger.
adapter_requirements: Deployment adapter implements run-scoped identity and ownership independently of messaging subject names and accelerator lease identity.
Runtime propagates the logical run identity through every created object.
cases.acceptance: RunA remains unchanged and correctly configured throughout runB creation/deletion, or runB is rejected before any mutation under an explicit single-run policy.

cases.title: Local supervision notices a later worker failure while an earlier worker stays alive
given: The local process list contains an indefinitely running source first and a processor second.
The supervisor has a configured failure-observation deadline S and a finite restart budget.
fault_schedule: Kill the second process after readiness while the first remains healthy and alive.
Repeat until restart budget exhaustion, then exercise the configured whole-run abort policy.
assertions: Failure detection does not block in wait() on the earlier source.
The failed processor is restarted or terminally classified within S plus declared scheduling tolerance.
Budget exhaustion emits the declared abort/failure outcome and does not leave a healthy source hiding a dead downstream worker.
evidence: Process IDs and exit times, supervisor observations/restarts, deadline measurements and terminal run events.
adapter_requirements: Runtime supervisor observes all worker lifecycles concurrently; allocation and messaging adapters expose failure/recovery hooks but do not own process-list ordering.
Worker readiness, process liveness and application completion remain separate states.
cases.acceptance: The later-process failure is handled within the declared observation deadline while the first process is still running, and exhaustion produces the specified terminal behavior.
